jobs.title: Marketing Technology Engineer
jobs.description:
Marketing Technology Engineer

Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

Marketing Operations owns the systems the marketing organization runs on: the MarTech stack, the data that describes our funnel, and increasingly the AI agents that do the work. The Marketing Technology Engineer owns the automation and AI layer of that stack — building the agents and automations that remove manual work from the team, and making sure they keep running and keep producing output we can trust. This is a technical role inside a marketing function, and the marketing half is not optional.

The impact you'll have here:

  • Own the operating layer for marketing's agent fleet end to end — provisioning, output verification, monitoring, alerting, and incident response. Nothing counts as shipped until it has run for real and its output has been checked.

  • Design and build agentic processes, skills, and automations that remove manual work from the team, and decide — with marketing judgment — which are worth building at all.

  • Instrument what we build so usage, output, and value are visible to leadership, and so agents improve from feedback rather than staying frozen at launch.

  • Consolidate how core marketing concepts are defined across tools and agents — territory, lead scoring stages, MQL and MQA, pipeline stages, targets — so automations and dashboards cannot quietly disagree, including across two product lines.

  • Own the MarTech stack — configuration, administration, and integration — and build in a way the campaign execution team can extend without engineering support for routine work.

What we're looking for:

  • Prior marketing or marketing operations experience — required, not preferred. You already understand funnel and attribution logic, lead scoring, send-cadence and deliverability norms, and list hygiene and consent rules. This role has no downstream reviewer for marketing correctness.

  • You have personally operated something unattended. A pipeline, integration, or agent that ran on its own, broke without telling you, and taught you to verify output rather than trust a green status. Scale matters less than the scar tissue.

  • A track record of building production automation inside a GTM function — Clay, Zapier, Workato, n8n, or similar — where what you built was depended on by other people and you were the one who owned it.

  • Evidence you have moved from no-code stitching into code and repository practice: version control, code review, CI, testing, and deploying into a shared repo rather than a personal account.

  • Technical baseline: working proficiency in SQL and Python, solid REST API fundamentals, familiarity with secrets management for credentials and API keys, enough data-warehouse fluency (for example BigQuery) to query and reason about data models, and hands-on administration of HubSpot and Salesforce.

Nice to have:

  • Direct experience with Claude, or with n8n.

  • Experience building multi-step enrichment waterfalls in Clay or similar that others depend on.

  • Exposure to observability or data-quality practices — monitoring, alerting, freshness and anomaly checks — in any prior role.

  • Experience supporting more than one product line, where the same metric has to be correct in two motions at once.

About the Team:

  • Marketing Operations is a distributed, not distant team that owns the systems the marketing organization runs on.

  • The work is intellectually difficult because the same metric has to stay correct across two product lines and multiple tools and agents at once.

  • Ownership is high: this role makes consequential marketing decisions without a downstream reviewer.

The following represents the expected range of compensation for this role:

  • Individual pay is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location. The compensation details listed in this posting reflect the US base salary only.

  • The estimated base salary range for this role is $150,000–$190,000 USD.

  • Additionally, this role may be eligible to participate in TRM’s equity plan.

  • Please note – we factor in the different costs for geographies outside the United States

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy.

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@trmlabs.com.

To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form.

Recruitment agencies

TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.

jobs.title: Head of Finance Automation/ AI Agentification
jobs.description:
Head of Finance Automation/ AI Agentification

Finance at Rohlik is being rebuilt to run on AI. We already have agents in production that chase overdue payments, process invoices, allocate cash and clear the team's inbox. The pieces work. What we need now is one person to own the whole thing and make it deliver at scale.

 

Role Overview

This is a new role that owns how AI and automation reshape the finance operating model across the Group. You will take a programme that is already live across procure to pay, order to cash and our shared services centre, and turn it from a set of promising experiments into the way finance actually runs.

You report to the Group CFO. You inherit a small team and a live roadmap, and you own the result. You decide what gets automated first, you build and ship with AI tools when that is the fastest way, and you hold every workstream to a number.

The role is deliberately hands on. You should be close enough to the work to build an agent or connect two systems through an API with AI assistance, even though you are not a software developer. You should also be senior enough to redesign how finance works and bring the rest of the business with you.

 

Why this role is exciting

  • You’ll inherit a live AI programme with real agents, real data and real impact from day one — not a greenfield slide deck.

  • You’ll shape how Finance actually runs across the Group as we move toward the next stage of growth — including the journey toward IPO readiness.

  • You’ll have access to a top-notch AI-first tech stack and the freedom to use it pragmatically.

  • You’ll work directly with the Group CFO, with fast decisions and no corporate red tape.

  • Your good ideas will be implemented almost immediately — not parked in a roadmap waiting for HQ approval.

  • You’ll lead a small team, but this is not a “manager from a distance” role. It’s highly hands-on, high-impact, and built for someone who wants to make things move fast.

 

What we expect from you

  • Own the AI and automation agenda across finance, from strategy through delivery to measured impact.

  • Lead process redesign the right way: map and understand the as-is, then design an agentic-first to-be rather than automating the old steps.

  • Lead complex cross-functional programmes across Finance, Tech and Operations, driving delivery through stakeholders and teams beyond your direct reporting line.

  • Bring the live programme to its targets, with a clear owner, baseline and deadline behind every workstream.

  • Redesign core finance processes around AI and agents, starting with close, reporting and forecasting.

  • Build and ship yourself when it is faster, using AI assisted tools to create agents and connect systems such as NetSuite, Rossum and n8n.

  • Lead and grow the team (three today) and raise AI fluency across finance and the SSC so the business can use what you build.

  • Track what matters and report it straight: automation rate, close time, cash allocation speed, cost and effort taken out.

  • Roll out across our five markets, balancing local reality against one Group standard.

 

What we look for

You have probably spent time in strategy consulting or in a transformation role, and you are now genuinely excited by what AI can do. You are a sharp generalist who can walk into a messy process, find the real problem, and fix it. You are as comfortable in a CFO pre-read as you are in the AI first tool building the thing.

  • A track record of leading transformation or automation programmes that actually delivered. A consulting, operations or generalist operator background all fit.

  • Strong understanding of finance processes, ideally gained through finance transformation, operating model redesign or automation programmes.

  • Hands on with AI. You can build agents and integrate APIs with AI assistance. You are not a software engineer and you do not need to be, but the tooling does not scare you.

  • You set baselines, name owners, hit deadlines, and say so early when something slips.

  • You can lead a small team and still do the work yourself.

  • You prioritise by impact and move fast. Better done than perfect.

  • You bring finance, tech and operations along with you.

  • Fluent in English. other languages will be an advantage.

  • Regular travel to Prague HQ required (min. 4 days per month)

What we offer

  • Great discounts through Corporate Benefits – fitness, travel, tickets, shopping and much more

  • Real growth: we’re not a traditional corporate.

As our Forward Deployed Engineer you are the technical face of comstruct - the person who turns a signed deal into a live and working systems for the customer.

But you'll also be on construction sites and in customer meetings regularly - onboarding teams, debugging their problems with the goal to drive every project from POV to full rollout and go-live.

You're a builder who'd rather talk to customers and solve real problems on real construction sites than polish code in isolation? Then we should talk.

Construction is one of the largest and least digitized industries in the world. We're building its digital future. Founded in March 2022, we've raised a €12.5M seed round from 20VC, Google Ventures and top European investors and nine of Switzerland's ten largest contractors already run on comstruct. That's the foundation. The category-defining company gets built now - together with you!

We’ve gone from zero to ten, now we’re looking to go from ten to one hundred!

jobs.description:
AI Engineer - Full time

TLDR; Davis is hiring an AI Engineer to work on the multi-agent pipeline turning raw, fragmented data into expert-grade real estate deliverables. You will make it more reliable, fast, and indistinguishable from the best human teams, then push it past what any human team could do, owning the stack end to end, from context engineering and orchestration to verification, storage and evaluation.

About Davis

Davis is an AI-native real estate company accelerating early-stage development and architectural design. Today developers coordinate 4-5 fragmented stakeholders over weeks or months. Soon they'll need only one: Davis.

We turn every input that shapes a development decision into decision-ready outputs: investor-grade feasibility studies, investment analysis, and architect-certified designs, delivered in days. Every stage pairs our proprietary AI systems with expert review, so velocity never comes at the cost of reliability.

We closed a $5.5M pre-seed co-led by Heartcore Capital and Balderton Capital, with Yellow, Evantic and Entrepreneur First, alongside angels from the founding teams of Spacemaker, Black Forest Labs, Hugging Face, Supabase, Cleo and Spore Bio. We already work with leading developers and expect to support hundreds of projects over the coming year, deepening our research, our hiring, and our coverage of the development process end to end.

Where We Operate

Early-stage development starts with a chain of high-stakes decisions, each requiring different data, different expertise, and different deliverables. Today, we deliver AI-powered outputs across the full spectrum - site sourcing, feasibility studies, architectural design, investment analysis, financial modeling, dataroom analysis, and more.

The Role

You will work on one of the core systems behind what Davis delivers. Our agents take raw, fragmented data and turn it into deliverables that real estate professionals use to make high-stakes decisions. Your job is to make that pipeline reliable, fast, and indistinguishable from work done by the best human teams - then push it beyond what any human team could do.

You can expect to:

  • Build and operate multi-agent systems that turn heterogeneous data into expert-grade deliverables across real estate development workflows.

  • Own the system end to end: infra, orchestration, context engineering, how the system selects, structures, and injects the right information so agents behave reliably at scale.

  • Ensure production-grade quality, performance, and reliability across every output we deliver to clients.

  • Sit with clients and domain experts regularly to understand their constraints, challenge your own assumptions, and make sure every output meets and even exceeds clients' expectations.

Beyond the technical depth, this role will expose you to how real estate decisions are made, how clients think, and what it takes to deliver outputs they trust. You'll develop a sharp business intuition alongside your engineering skills.

Key Responsibilities

  • Harness engineering: design and build the system layer around the model - context assembly, tool orchestration, verification, and report generation - to deliver consistent, high-quality outputs at scale.

  • Data ingestion & context assembly: handle messy, unstructured project data from heterogeneous sources and ensure agents have the right context at all times.

  • Storage & traceability: persist sources, extracted facts, intermediate results, report versions, and expert edits.

  • Expert-in-the-loop UX: design and build the review experience (annotations, edits, approvals, diffs/version history, provenance display).

  • Evaluation & benchmarking: build an internal eval harness (datasets, rubrics, regression tests, monitoring) to track agents performance over time.

What We're Looking For

  • 1.5+ years building and deploying production software at scale (APIs, reliability, testing, performance).

  • Experience building and evaluating LLM agents / multi-step workflows in real systems.

  • Proven context engineering experience: you've built systems where reliability depends on assembling the right context (RAG over heterogeneous sources, summarization, conversation state, tool outputs).

  • Deep Python expertise (clean architecture, typing, async/concurrency, strong testing culture).

  • Strong experience with databases + data modeling (structured storage, document storage, versioning).

  • Full-stack experience (you can ship a real UI), with a clear backend emphasis.

  • Comfortable building from first principles: we don't want heavy agent frameworks — we prefer a lightweight, well-engineered codebase.

Nice to Have

  • Experience operating LLM systems with observability and quality monitoring in production.

  • GIS familiarity (parcels, zoning layers, geocoding).

  • Multi-country product experience (heterogeneous sources, localization, varying rules).

  • NLP background

Why Join Us

You're joining a team of 9 at the very beginning - where every decision you make shapes the product, the culture, and the trajectory of the company. What you build here will be yours.

  • Direct impact on growth: your work doesn't sit behind three layers of review. You ship, clients use it, and you see the results. Every output you improve translates directly into revenue and reputation.

  • Real-world impact: your work supports investment decisions, accelerates development timelines, and helps redefine how cities are imagined, designed, and built.

  • High ownership: own the full feasibility stack end to end, as the CEO of that part.

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity in an early-stage company.

  • A small team with high standards - we ship fast and love working together.

More information about Davis, the team and the market we’re going after:

Team

Mehdi (Co-founder & CEO) grew up in a family of architects and has lived this problem firsthand. Data Center Architect

TLDR; Davis is looking for an architect who has already run data center feasibility studies on their own, and who can answer the question a client asks in front of a site: how many megawatts can this land absorb. We expect three to five years on the data center product, with two or three projects seen end to end.

We already work with leading developers and expect to support hundreds of projects over the coming year, deepening our research, our hiring, and our coverage of the development process end to end.

The Role

The data center market is structuring fast, operators and landowners are hunting for sites, and the question they ask is one of capacity: how many megawatts of IT load does this land carry, under what scheme, and on what conditions. We answer in days where the market takes weeks. You will be the person who answers for that number.

You will run a portfolio of test fits and data center feasibility studies, with occasional work on large logistics and industry. Under the supervision of a lead architect, you take these projects from first capacity through to schematic design, and you present them to the client.

The core of the role

  • Establish a site's capacity in IT megawatts, working from the local zoning rules and operating constraints, and set out the assumptions behind it.

  • Qualify the applicable land-use category and the environmental-classification regime for industrial facilities, and derive from them the permitted height, the setbacks and the siting conditions.

  • Draw the data halls at their real grid, fully laid out, with their aisles, their air-handling units and their structural grid.

  • Compose the industrial site plan: service yards, a perimeter heavy-vehicle road, loading docks, retention basins, planted buffers, access and parking.

  • Arbitrate between schemes, one level, two levels or more, while respecting the slab-to-slab height and the zoning height cap.

  • Name the questions to put to the operator: cooling system, density per rack, electrical redundancy, hall dimensions, height.

  • Carry your number in front of the client, and defend it under challenge.

  • Place the project on its critical path: grid connection, environmental permitting, ecological surveys, preventive archaeology.

Contribute to the technology

  • Formalize data center best practice, translating the sizing cascade, the grids and the thresholds into criteria our AI teams can use.

  • Qualify the model's outputs, saying what is right, what is wrong, and on what grounds.

  • Work across the product, tech and real estate teams, inside the tool's continuous-improvement cycles.

Work as a team

  • Take part in project reviews and exchange with the other architects to improve the methods and the quality of the deliverables.

  • Contribute to the team's graphic standards.

What We’re Looking For

  • Education: a degree in architecture.

  • Experience: we count projects as much as years. Three to five years on the data center product, with two or three projects seen across their full cycle. One of them should be a project you carried yourself, from capacity through to permit or schematic design. A background in large logistics or industrial buildings is a valid base, provided you add that data center experience to it.

  • Software: mastery of Rhino and Revit is essential, and AutoCAD is expected.

  • Appetite for digital tools and AI: you do not need to code, but the drive to fold these tools into your practice and push it forward is essential.

  • Speed and synthesis: our clients decide fast, on a number. You need to produce a credible, well-drawn scenario in hours, cut to the essential on ambiguous cases, and know what level of detail serves the decision at each phase.

Domain skills

  • Product knowledge, the sizing cascade of a data center, hall, power, cooling, telecom and logistics, the slab-to-slab height and what it imposes, the rack-and-aisle grid, electrical redundancy, the order of magnitude of a PUE.

  • Applied regulatory fluency, the land-use sub-category and the 2023 ruling that reclassified data centers, the environmental-classification headings and the threshold that triggers a full environmental permit, height and setback rules, no-net-land-take targets and designation as a project of major national interest, rooftop renewable-energy requirements.

  • Buildable capacity, linking a rule to its quantified effect on a volume, and a volume to an installable power.

  • Industrial site planning, heavy-vehicle access, turning circles, fire safety, water management, insertion and edges.

  • Graphic production, plans, sections and diagrams that make a capacity argument legible to an investor.

  • Ownership of the subject, presenting, arguing and defending a number in front of a client who contests it. We are looking for someone who has owned the subject end to end, assumptions, number and client presentation.

Complementary skills

  • Rigor and a sense of synthesis, especially on ambiguous cases.

  • Structuring information, organizing what you produce so that others, human or machine, can use it.

  • An ability to work across the product, tech and real estate teams.

  • A command of technical English, the vocabulary of the sector being largely English-speaking.

Why Join Davis?

  • Take part in a genuine transformation of the real estate profession, and co-build the next generation of feasibility standards alongside a high-caliber technical team.

  • You will set Davis's data center method, and it will serve every project that follows.

  • See your work in every deliverable, and correct the tool when it gets things wrong.

  • Join a young company, where the methods and the tools are still being built, and where your expertise shapes the way we work.

Product Manager – Agent Experience ( Français/ Anglais)

Product Manager – Agent Experience

Lieu : Paris de préférence, possibilité à Londres (hybride, trois jours par semaine au bureau)
Équipe : Customer Care
Langues : Maîtrise du français et de l’anglais
Contrat : CDI
Rattachement : Lead Product Manager

À noter : ce poste est ouvert à Paris et à Londres, et nécessite un droit de travailler déjà acquis dans le pays où vous serez basé(e) (UE pour Paris, Royaume-Uni pour Londres). Nous ne pouvons pas proposer de parrainage de visa, mais nous étudions le parrainage poste par poste : gardez un œil sur notre site carrières pour de futures opportunités.

Merci de soumettre votre CV en anglais.

À propos de Kaluza

Kaluza est la plateforme d’Energy Intelligence qui transforme la complexité de l’énergie en coordination fluide. Nous aidons les énergéticiens à relever les défis d’aujourd’hui tout en accélérant la transition vers un avenir propre et électrifié.

Notre plateforme orchestre des millions de décisions en temps réel entre les foyers, les appareils, les marchés et les réseaux. En associant algorithmes prédictifs et conception centrée sur l’humain, Kaluza rend l’énergie propre fiable, abordable et adaptée à la vie de tous les jours.

Avec des équipes en Europe, en Asie et en Australie, et une joint-venture avec Mitsubishi Corporation au Japon, nous accompagnons des acteurs majeurs comme OVO, AGL et ENGIE, ainsi que des entreprises innovantes comme Volvo et Volkswagen.

Ce que vous ferez

  • Piloter la roadmap : porter la stratégie de bout en bout de Kaluza Agent Experience (KAE) sur le marché européen, en cohérence avec les objectifs produit globaux et affinée par les besoins clients locaux et les comportements des agents. Vous suivrez les indicateurs opérationnels clés (AHT, FCR, CSAT, adoption de l’IA, onboarding) pour vous assurer que chaque évolution améliore l’expérience des agents et des clients.

  • Concevoir les parcours et garantir la cohérence UX : être le garant de l’expérience agent sur l’ensemble de KAE. Vous travaillerez avec les équipes UX et métier pour appliquer des patterns communs, réduire la charge cognitive des agents et rester aligné avec le design system, y compris quand de nouvelles capacités d’automatisation et d’assistance par l’IA sont introduites.

  • Mener les intégrations et l’onboarding client : piloter les intégrations techniques et produit avec des plateformes tierces, et superviser de bout en bout le déploiement de nouvelles instances KAE pour les nouveaux clients, de la phase de découverte jusqu’à la mise en production.

  • Garantir l’accessibilité et la conformité : défendre les réglementations européennes d’accessibilité dès la conception, en traduisant les exigences réglementaires et spécifiques à chaque marché en besoins techniques concrets.

  • Accompagner les clients et créer de la valeur : être l’expert de confiance des clients sur l’expérience agent, en défendant une configuration native de la plateforme plutôt que des développements sur mesure.

  • Rester les mains dans le cambouis, de la livraison à l’accompagnement : vous impliquer sur l’ensemble du cycle de vie du développement produit (PDLC), des sessions de discovery avec les agents aux boucles de feedback, et produire les supports qui favorisent l’adoption côté clients.

(À noter : des déplacements chez les clients, par exemple à Bruxelles, sont à prévoir, environ 1 à 3 par mois au début, puis 1 à 2 par trimestre.)

Ce que vous apporterez

Idéalement, vous avez :

  • Une expertise centres de contact et UX : une solide expérience de la responsabilité de parcours utilisateurs de bout en bout pour des outils opérationnels très sollicités (par exemple des postes de travail d’agents), avec une vraie pratique de la recherche utilisateur, de la cartographie de parcours et des tests d’usabilité auprès d’agents et de superviseurs.

  • Une connaissance de l’accessibilité européenne et de l’intégration de plateformes : une bonne maîtrise des standards d’accessibilité européens, ainsi qu’une expérience avérée d’intégration de produits avec des plateformes tierces et des écosystèmes de fournisseurs complexes.

  • Une expérience de delivery client et d’expansion de marché : un historique de mise en œuvre ou de localisation d’un produit pour des clients entreprise externes, en menant les solutions de zéro à la mise en production : discovery, configuration et conduite du changement.

  • Un jugement fondé sur la donnée et de l’influence : la capacité démontrée à vous appuyer sur des indicateurs opérationnels (AHT, FCR, CSAT, effort de l’agent) pour défendre vos décisions produit, avec un état d’esprit « plateforme d’abord » qui privilégie les capacités existantes au code sur mesure.

  • Un bilinguisme professionnel : une maîtrise complète, à l’écrit comme à l’oral, du français et de l’anglais.

Ce qui fera la différence

  • Une expérience de l’utilisation d’outils d’IA, de capacités de machine learning ou d’intégrations LLM dans des workflows produit, pour renforcer l’intelligence de la plateforme et l’automatisation directement dans les environnements de poste de travail du service client.

  • Une expérience dans des plateformes SaaS, le secteur de l’énergie ou des migrations d’envergure chez des opérateurs de services publics.

  • Une expérience concrète de la mise à l’échelle de la cohérence UI entre plusieurs équipes produit.

Où vous travaillerez

Nous proposons un cadre de travail flexible, avec trois jours par semaine au bureau. C’est le meilleur des deux mondes : du temps réel ensemble pour collaborer et créer des liens, et la liberté de travailler comme vous le préférez le reste de la semaine.

Nos valeurs

Cinq valeurs guident notre façon de travailler chez Kaluza :

  • Jouer pour gagner : la fierté collective de décarboner l’énergie à grande échelle.

  • Résoudre le vrai problème : aller droit au but pour se concentrer sur des résultats concrets.

jobs.title: SMB Account Executive
jobs.description:
SMB Account Executive

We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

ROLE OVERVIEW

We are seeking a motivated and results-driven SMB Account Executive to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for driving new business within the EMEA territory, focusing on building and maintaining strong relationships with key stakeholders across various personas within small and medium-sized accounts. You will play a crucial role in expanding our customer base and ensuring successful sales outcomes through effective pipeline generation and accurate sales forecasting.

 

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Pipeline Generation: Enthusiastically creating and driving your own pipeline by identifying new business opportunities and engaging multiple personas from scientists to C-suite. Utilize various strategies and tools to generate leads and move them through the sales cycle.

  • Sales Forecasting: Develop and maintain accurate sales forecasts (+/- 10 of goal), leveraging data to inform decision-making and ensure predictable revenue outcomes with the goal of consistent attainment of revenue targets.

  • Solution Selling: Effectively communicate the value of our platform, tailoring presentations and proposals to meet the specific needs of each prospect.

  • Platform Demonstrations: Running Benchling platform demonstrations aligned to a clear customer problem statement and a Benchling proven solution to potential clients to help clients understand the value of Benchling to them specifically.

  • Negotiation and Closing: Lead negotiations with potential clients, by thoughtfully addressing key stakeholders including multiple personas and CxO in the buyer journey, while navigating organizational complexities, addressing objections and securing new business agreements.

  • Account Engagement: Work across multiple personas within an account to understand their unique needs and align Benchling’s solutions with their business objectives.

  • Collaboration: Partner with internal teams (marketing, product, customer success, etc) and Channel to ensure a seamless experience for clients and drive long-term customer satisfaction.

  • Continuous Learning: Stay informed about industry trends, competitors, and emerging technologies to maintain a competitive edge in the market.

  • Process: Drive the sales process through Pipeline Generation (PG), 3 Why’s, Champion Building, MEDDIC, Command of the Message, etc. Maintain account integrity and opportunity data within company systems; Salesforce 

QUALIFICATIONS

You are drawn to our mission and you want to help Benchling win new business. You are committed to working in a collaborative environment, working together as a team. You have a love for working in a fast-paced environment and taking the initiative to get stuff done and try new things. You are passionate about powering new possibilities in biotech faster.

  • Bachelor’s degree - life sciences major is required.

  • 1-3 years of experience as an Account Executive, Field Application Scientist, Account Manager. Sales Development Background highly appreciated.

  • Demonstrable history of consistently achieving or exceeding ambitious sales targets.

  • Curiosity, creativity, and persistence. You should be excited to collaborate with customers as a thought partner.

  • Dynamic communication skills and the versatility to connect effectively with a range of stakeholders, including scientists, team project leads and executives in industry. 

HOW WE WORK

We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday).

SALARY & BENEFITS

Full-time employees outside the U.S. enjoy a comprehensive benefits program tailored to their region of residence.

jobs.title: IT Reliability Engineer
jobs.description:
IT Reliability Engineer

Du möchtest Verantwortung übernehmen, moderne IT-Umgebungen zuverlässig betreiben und den Bereich IT Reliability Engineering aktiv mit aufbauen?

Als IT Reliability Engineer bist du Teil unseres Engineering-Teams und übernimmst die Verantwortung für die Stabilität, Überwachung und kontinuierliche Verbesserung bestehender Kundenumgebungen.

Du sorgst dafür, dass Systeme zuverlässig betrieben werden, technische Risiken frühzeitig erkannt werden und Monitoring-, Backup-, Update- sowie Lifecycle-Prozesse nachhaltig funktionieren. Dabei leistest du einen wichtigen Beitrag zur Servicequalität und zur langfristigen Stabilität unserer Kundenumgebungen.

Die Themen Monitoring, Betriebsstabilität, Lifecycle-Management und technische Qualitätsstandards haben bei MDigital bereits heute einen hohen Stellenwert und werden aktiv durch unser Engineering-Team gelebt. Aufgrund des Unternehmenswachstums und der zunehmenden Bedeutung dieser Aufgaben investieren wir nun gezielt in eine spezialisierte Rolle innerhalb des Engineering-Teams.

Da diese Position neu geschaffen wird, hast du die Möglichkeit, die zukünftige Ausgestaltung der Rolle aktiv mitzuprägen. Mit dem weiteren Wachstum des Unternehmens besteht zudem die Perspektive, den Bereich IT Reliability Engineering langfristig weiter auszubauen und zusätzliche Mitarbeitende in diesem Umfeld zu etablieren.

Aufgaben

Monitoring & Infrastruktur

  • Überwachung sämtlicher Kundensysteme über unsere Monitoring-Plattformen
  • Analyse, Priorisierung und Nachverfolgung von Warnmeldungen
  • Sicherstellung der vollständigen Integration produktiver Systeme ins Monitoring
  • Überwachung von Verfügbarkeit, Diensten, Hardware- und Storage-Zuständen
  • Frühzeitige Erkennung technischer und sicherheitsrelevanter Risiken
  • Eskalation kritischer Ereignisse
  • Kontinuierliche Verbesserung und Weiterentwicklung bestehender Monitoring-Prozesse
  • Identifikation und Umsetzung von Verbesserungen zur Erhöhung der Betriebsstabilität
  • Förderung von Standardisierung und Automatisierung im täglichen Betrieb
  • Analyse wiederkehrender Incidents und Erarbeitung nachhaltiger Lösungen

Backup & Recovery

  • Sicherstellung funktionierender Backup- und Recovery-Prozesse
  • Nachverfolgung fehlerhafter Sicherungen
  • Integration neuer Systeme in bestehende Backup-Konzepte
  • Planung, Durchführung und Dokumentation regelmässiger Restore-Tests

Client-, Server- & Update-Management

  • Überwachung des Update- und Sicherheitsstatus von Clients und Servern
  • Sicherstellung aktueller Sicherheits- und Systemstände
  • Standardisierung und Automatisierung von Update-Prozessen
  • Verwaltung von Serversystemen über Microsoft Azure Arc
  • Verwaltung von Clients über Microsoft Intune und bestehende Endpoint-Management-Lösungen
  • Förderung einer möglichst zentralisierten und automatisierten Systemverwaltung

Evergreen & Lifecycle Management

  • Überwachung von EOL- und EOS-Systemen
  • Kontrolle von Firmware-, Software- und Security-Ständen
  • Identifikation technischer und sicherheitsrelevanter Altlasten
  • Erarbeitung von Handlungsempfehlungen für Engineering und Management
  • Unterstützung von Standardisierungsinitiativen

Lizenz-, Zertifikats- & Vertragsüberwachung

  • Überwachung von SSL-Zertifikaten und Laufzeiten
  • Kontrolle von Softwarelizenzen und Wartungsverträgen
  • Frühzeitige Meldung bevorstehender Verlängerungen
  • Vermeidung betrieblicher Risiken durch ablaufende Lizenzen oder Zertifikate
  • Nachvollziehbare Dokumentation relevanter Informationen

Dokumentation & Betriebsqualität

  • Pflege und Weiterentwicklung technischer Kundendokumentationen
  • Erstellung und Aktualisierung von Betriebsanleitungen
  • Dokumentation neuer Systeme und Änderungen
  • Sicherstellung eines nachvollziehbaren und professionellen Betriebsstandards
  • Unterstützung bei der Kommunikation kritischer technischer Ereignisse

Pikettdienst und Team-Integration

Als Teil unseres Engineering-Teams beteiligst du dich am rotierenden Pikettdienst und hilfst mit, den stabilen Betrieb unserer Kundenumgebungen auch ausserhalb der regulären Arbeitszeiten sicherzustellen. Die Teilnahme am Pikettdienst wird entsprechend geplant und vergütet.

Bei Bedarf unterstützt du zusätzlich das Engineering-Team bei Rollouts, technischen Umsetzungen oder klar definierten Projektaufgaben was zusätzliche Abwechslung mit sich bringt. Der Schwerpunkt bleibt jedoch bewusst auf der Sicherstellung eines professionellen Betriebs unserer Kundenumgebungen ausgerichtet.

Qualifikation

Das zeichnet Dich aus

  • Du übernimmst gerne Verantwortung und möchtest aktiv etwas aufbauen und mitgestalten.
  • Du arbeitest strukturiert, zuverlässig und nachhaltig.
  • Du erkennst Risiken frühzeitig und kommunizierst diese verständlich.
  • Du hast Freude daran, Systeme stabil und sicher zu betreiben.
  • Du interessierst dich für Monitoring, Automatisierung und Prozessverbesserungen.
  • Du schätzt klare Standards und professionelle Betriebsprozesse.
  • Du arbeitest gerne selbstständig und denkst unternehmerisch.

Fachliche Qualifikationen

  • Erfahrung im Bereich System Engineering, IT-Betrieb, Managed Services, Monitoring oder Infrastruktur
  • Gute Kenntnisse in Microsoft 365, Microsoft Azure, Windows Server und Netzwerktechnologien
  • Grundlegendes Verständnis von IT-Security und Cyber-Risiken
  • Erfahrung mit Monitoring-Lösungen von Vorteil
  • Kenntnisse im Bereich Backup- und Recovery-Lösungen
  • Erfahrung mit Microsoft Intune oder vergleichbaren Endpoint-Management-Lösungen
  • Kenntnisse von Microsoft Azure Arc von Vorteil
  • Strukturierte, selbstständige und verantwortungsbewusste Arbeitsweise

  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse
  • Führerausweis Kategorie B

Zertifizierungen

Folgende Zertifizierungen sind vorhanden oder deren Erreichung wird gemeinsam vereinbart. Die Zertifizierungskosten werden durch uns übernommen.

  • Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900)
  • Microsoft Azure Administrator (AZ-104)

Von Vorteil

  • Sophos Central Endpoint and Server Protection
  • Veeam Certified Engineer (VMCE)
  • Weitere Microsoft-, Sophos- oder Security-Zertifizierungen

Benefits

Aufbau eines neuen Fachbereichs

Du übernimmst nicht einfach eine bestehende Rolle, sondern gestaltest den Bereich IT Reliability Engineering bei MDigital aktiv mit. Deine Ideen, Erfahrungen und Verbesserungen fliessen direkt in die Weiterentwicklung von Prozessen, Standards und Arbeitsweisen ein.

Hohe Eigenverantwortung

Du erhältst ein hohes Mass an Vertrauen, Verantwortung und Gestaltungsspielraum und übernimmst eine zentrale Rolle für die Stabilität und Qualität unserer Kundenumgebungen.

Moderne Technologien

Arbeite mit Microsoft Azure, Azure Arc, Microsoft Intune, Site24x7, Sophos, Veeam und weiteren modernen Plattformen.

Weiterbildung & Zertifizierungen

Wir fördern deine fachliche und persönliche Weiterentwicklung durch Schulungen, Zertifizierungen und praxisnahe Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten.

Entwicklungsperspektiven

Mit dem Wachstum des Unternehmens besteht die Möglichkeit, den Bereich IT Reliability Engineering weiter auszubauen und künftig zusätzliche Mitarbeitende fachlich zu begleiten oder ein eigenes Team mit aufzubauen.

Firmenfahrzeug

Für Kundentermine und Projekteinsätze stehen Dir Firmenfahrzeuge zur geschäftlichen Nutzung zur Verfügung. Du arbeitest dort, wo Resultate entstehen – im direkten Austausch mit den Kunden.

Weiterentwicklung garantiert

Wir investieren gezielt in Dich. Du arbeitest mit modernen Technologien wie Azure, Intune, Veeam oder Sophos und wirst aktiv in deiner Entwicklung unterstützt – inkl. Zeitbudget für Zertifizierungen und Trainings.

Professionelles Arbeitsumfeld

Strukturierte Arbeitsweise, klare Abläufe und nachvollziehbare Verantwortung. Home-Office ist möglich, wird aber als Mittel zum Ergebnis verstanden – Verantwortung hat Priorität.

Starke Rahmenbedingungen

40-Stunden-Woche, 30 Tage Ferien, pauschale Mobile-Spesen und moderne Arbeitsmittel gehören bei uns dazu.

Einsatzort

Diese Position richtet sich an Bewerberinnen und Bewerber mit Wohnsitz in der Schweiz oder im angrenzenden Ausland (Grenzregionen Deutschland, Österreich, Frankreich). Die Rolle beinhaltet regelmässige Kundenbesuche, die Teilnahme am Pikettdienst sowie eine enge Zusammenarbeit mit unserem Engineering-Team.

jobs.title: Quantum Processor Development Lead
jobs.description:
Quantum Processor Development Lead

About Us

QuantWare is building the world’s most powerful quantum processors to solve humanity's greatest challenges. We do this with our unique VIO™ technology, the only QPU architecture that breaks the hardware barriers that have held quantum computing back, unlocking the path to MegaQubit quantum processors.

With VIO, we are paving the way for the hyper-scale quantum computers that will change the world. And delivering on that vision demands people who don’t shy away from tackling the hardest challenges of our time. That’s where you come in!

As a Quantum Processor Development Lead you own people management and project leadership for our quantum processor developement. You rapidly grow the team by recruiting key members, while maintaining a high level of care and support for the team members. You report to the VP of Product and work closely with them to shape the team that defines the direction of key technical development at QuantWare. You will work with some of the smartest and most passionate people in the field, helping us build the world's most powerful quantum processors, as fast as possible.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Own and drive processor development

    • Manage development work - particularly chip design and cryogenic measurement.

    • Run smaller, self-contained projects within your team - supporting both department and company-wide initiatives.

    • Partner with assigned Program Managers on larger, cross-department programs, particularly regarding technical execution and requirements compliance of QPUs.

  • Manage uncertainty and technical risk

    • Identify technical risks and bottlenecks early

    • Plan for potential failure modes and contingencies

    • Adapt experimental strategies dynamically based on new information

  • Develop engineering practices within the team

    • Develop a deep technical understanding of quantum processor technology to guide sound, well-informed decisions.

    • Implement strong and lean technical processes that support sound decision making processes. For example: requirements flowdown, trade studies, root cause corrective action methods, etc.

  • Support growth and development of the team

    • Contribute to defining role profiles and act as hiring manager for new roles across the programme.

    • Mentor engineers and project leads in programme execution and collaborative leadership.

    • Manage the engineers in your technology area: hire, coach, review performance, and grow careers.

Your Profile

  • Technical background

    • MSc, PhD, or equivalent experience in physics, electrical engineering, microwave/RF engineering, semiconductor technology, or a related field.

    • Understanding of the development lifecycle for chip-level technologies; experience with superconducting qubits or cryogenic systems is a strong plus.

  • Leadership experience

    • 4+ years delivering complex, research-intensive chip hardware projects in a project management capacity.

    • Show people-management experience: hiring, coaching, and performance management.

    • Lead projects as part of a larger program, with control over one’s own domain.

    • Run smaller projects directly, without needing dedicated program-management support.

    • Proven ability to work with highly specialised technical experts.

    • Experience working in a fast-moving start-up or scale-up environment balancing hands-on technical leadership with growing a team, as a strong plus.

  • Approach

    • Translate a long-term technical strategy into an execution plan for your team.

    • Strong analytical skills with the ability to make pragmatic, informed decisions under uncertainty.

    • Draw a clear line between technical leadership and program management, and partner with Program Managers instead of duplicating their function.

  • Communication

    • Excellent communicator who can motivate teams, facilitate alignment, adept at communicating technical ideas.

    • Communicate fluently in English.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway! Research shows women often self-select out if they don't meet every requirement. Here's our take: nobody ticks every box. This is a description of our ideal candidate, not a filter. If most resonates and you're keen to learn the gaps, apply. We hire for trajectory, not perfection.

What We Offer:

At QuantWare, you’ll be part of a high-performing team of world-class experts in an ambitious, fast-moving environment. From day one, you’ll have the trust, tools, and support to do your best work. Here’s what you can expect:

Competitive salary - A salary that reflects the impact and importance of the role (and of course 8% holiday allowance)

Pension that’s built to last - A generous and future-proof pension plan that includes partner and dependent coverage.

Flexibility built on trust - We focus on outcomes. Work flexibly, in a hybrid setup, with an open vacation policy that lets you manage your time

Personal growth - We invest in your L&D, with a budget available to each team member, dependent on their individual ambitions, development needs, and performance

A connected team - We make space to celebrate wins together, with team events, offsites, and spontaneous moments that bring us closer

Diversity & Inclusion at QuantWare

We’re an ambitious company, not only for our goals but also to become an even more diverse and inclusive team. We know great candidates don't always follow a straight path, and we value diverse experience, perspectives, and ways of thinking. We know this helps us make better decisions, drives more innovation, and strengthens our culture.

Water, bodem, ecologie, een primaire waterkering én verschillende partijen met ieder hun eigen verantwoordelijkheid en expertise. Je eigen netwerk zet je in om de dienstverlening van Waalpartners verder te profileren. Als projectleider ben je bovendien de spil in de ontwikkeling van zowel medewerkers als de organisatie.

Dat doe je niet alleen: samen schop je ‘t verder. Je werkt nauw samen met het management en de overige projectleiders over offertes, de bureauplanning en kansen in de markt.

Je bent open, nieuwsgierig en staat als leidinggevende stevig in je schoenen. Je omgeving ziet je als collegiaal en je neemt verantwoordelijkheid over je project en de ontwikkeling van de projectteamleden.

jobs.title: Specialist Account Executive, Sec Ops
SMB Account Executive (New Business)

Senior Business Controller (Operations)
jobs.description:
Senior Business Controller (Operations)

Would you like to work closely with the business as a Senior Business Controller and use your financial expertise to make a real impact on decisions? You will bring financial structure and insight, while keeping a forward-looking perspective: where can we improve, which decisions will make a financial difference, and what will they mean for our results?

HG is a compact, international organisation. This means considerable responsibility, direct contact with decision-makers and room to drive change yourself. We are therefore looking for someone who takes ownership, works pragmatically and is not afraid to challenge existing ways of working.

You will be based at our head office in Almere. Hybrid working opportunities are limited: regular office attendance is important in this role because of the close collaboration with Finance, Operations and other stakeholders. You will also travel to the United Kingdom or Germany several times a year.

About the role

As Senior Business Controller, you will be responsible for business control within Operations and will also support our subsidiaries in the United Kingdom and Germany. You have a clear vision of what the best operational business control model looks like and have proven experience in realizing this. The Senior Business Controller plays a key role in strengthening financial control, transparency and decision-making across Operations. The scope covers procurement and product costing, as well as warehouse and transport operations. Working closely with Finance, Procurement and Operations, the Senior Business Controller translates operational developments and improvement initiatives into clear financial insights and P&L impact

Our business is undergoing significant change. HG has recently changed its logistics service arrangements, consolidating most local warehouses into one central location as part of a cost-saving initiative. At the same time, a new ERP system is being implemented. This creates an interesting and dynamic environment in which existing budget models, cost allocation models, reporting and financial processes need to be further developed to reflect the new operating model and provide a solid basis for financial control and decision-making.

What you will do

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Owning the operational cost lines between Net Sales and Contribution Margin for the whole group and. act as a strong Finance business partner to the Chief Operating Officer and his team, translating operational developments into actionable financial insights;

  • Identifying and driving continuous improvements to the operational business, improving insights while reducing costs.

  • Being the financial business partner for the country managers in the UK and Germany, including reviewing commercial deals and business cases.

  • Analyzing budget versus actuals and explaining significant variances.

  • Developing a clear understanding of budgeted versus actual purchase prices and identifying the key drivers behind price variances.

  • Providing insight into raw material and purchase price developments and translating these into expected P&L impact.

  • Quantifying and tracking the financial impact of Procurement and product-costing initiatives and other savings programmes.

  • Establishing and further developing standard COGS based on expected cost developments.

  • Build a thorough understanding of the warehouse and distribution budget, operational performance and key savings initiatives. 

  • Track whether the expected savings from the recently implemented warehouse and transport provider change are being realized in the P&L. 

  • Further developing cost allocation models for individual markets, using meaningful drivers, and working towards more complete and reliable management reporting.

  • Ensuring the Operations P&L, budget and actual costs are consistently captured and reported in the same structure.

  • Translating inventory developments into financial impact and creating a clear link between stock levels, budget assumptions and cost allocation.

  • Supporting and improving an efficient month-end closing process, ensuring Operations costs are accurately and consistently booked, allocated and reconciled.

  • Establish or improve proper accounting entries together with Finance Administration and relevant operational partners.

  • Co-lead the annual budget cycle and budget presentations to the Board.

  • Using and improving Power BI, ERP data and financial processes to reduce manual work and increase transparency.

You will report directly to the Chief Financial Officer and work closely with colleagues in Finance, Procurement and Operations. You will also have regular contact with the Germany and UK country managers.

This position requires more than strong analytical skills. You will need to explain your insights clearly, engage stakeholders and constructively challenge where necessary. You will be a knowledgeable sparring partner who asks questions, brings structure and takes responsibility from analysis through to implementation. You proactively identify opportunities to improve financial processes, controls, reporting and transparency across Operations.

HG is a compact, fast-growing and international organization where you can directly see the impact of your work. This requires ownership, initiative and a pragmatic, results-oriented mindset. The team culture is open, pragmatic and focused on results, encouraging you to bring ideas forward, challenge constructively and take responsibility. Everything we do is guided by our three core values: Aim High, Be Brave, Be Connected.


What you bring

We are looking for a financially strong, hands-on and improvement-oriented controller who combines analytical capability with a practical understanding of Operations. The ideal candidate is comfortable working across Finance, Procurement and Operations and is able to turn complex cost drivers into clear insights and concrete actions.

What do we offer

You can expect:

Senior Security Operations Engineer

A little about us…Fleetio is a modern software platform that helps thousands of organizations worldwide manage their fleet operations. We raised $450M in our Series D funding round in March of 2025 and are on an exciting trajectory as a company. Fleetio is also a proud founding member of the Rails Foundation!

Description

Our Business Technology team is looking for a Senior Security Operations Engineer to own the security of the tools, devices, identities, and data Fleetians rely on every day. You will help run corporate security operations end to end, covering detection and response, identity, endpoint, email, and SaaS security, data loss prevention, AI security, and vulnerability management, and make the day-to-day security calls that keep Fleetio safe.

You will be hands-on: engineering controls, writing and tuning detections, automating response, and closing gaps, not just administering tools. The goal is one connected defense, not a collection of consoles: a signal from Okta, CrowdStrike, Mimecast, or Google Workspace should drive action in the others automatically, so the environment protects itself and people step in only where judgment is needed. Around-the-clock monitoring is handled by our external SOC (CrowdStrike Falcon Complete); this role engineers the environment it watches, owns what happens when it escalates, and extends what it can see. You will work closely with our IT Operations and Compliance teams, our 3rd party SOC, and the Product Security team in Platform Engineering.

Our team treats AI as a core part of how we work. We build and use AI agents and automated workflows to handle toil, speed up investigation and response, and give our team more time for high-leverage work.

Who You Are

Our ideal candidate is a security engineer who likes to build. You are as comfortable writing a detection or a response playbook as you are working an incident. You think in systems: you see the gaps between tools and close them by wiring the tools together. You make sound security decisions on your own, explain them clearly to technical and non-technical people, and balance risk with how people actually work.

You stay calm when something breaks. You can take a vague report, work out quickly what happened and who is affected, and give leaders a clear, evidence-backed answer. Then you fix the root cause so it doesn't happen the same way twice.

You're curious about how AI is changing security operations, and you're eager to put it to work on triage, enrichment, and response.

Your Impact

As a Senior Security Operations Engineer on Fleetio's Business Technology team, you will:

  • Own detection engineering and threat hunting in CrowdStrike Next-Gen SIEM: onboard log sources, write and tune detections across identity, email, SaaS, and endpoint telemetry, and keep false positives down
  • Own security automation: chain our tools together through CrowdStrike Fusion SOAR and our workflow automation platform so a signal in one (a risky Okta sign-in, a Falcon detection, a Mimecast hit, a Google Workspace sharing change) triggers enrichment, containment, paging, and ticketing in the others, plus AI agents that speed up triage and investigation, so routine response runs without waiting on a human
  • Lead corporate incident response as technical lead, including third-party and supply-chain events: scope exposure quickly, confirm or rule out compromise, run forensics, tell leaders and employees what to do, keep runbooks current with Product Security, and serve in the escalation rotation, backing up the Incident Commander when needed
  • Own CrowdStrike Falcon configuration and detections, manage the Falcon Complete relationship and escalations, and maintain device trust checks and an inventory of software and extensions on company devices with clear guidance on approved tools
  • Own Okta authentication policy, MFA, session policy, and privileged access management, and automate user access reviews and audit evidence with Compliance so SOC 2 controls run with less manual effort
  • Own Mimecast policy, secure network access, Google Workspace and key SaaS security settings, and SaaS security posture in CrowdStrike Falcon Shield, driving findings to closure with app owners
  • Own data loss prevention: define and classify Fleetio's sensitive data, design and tune DLP policies across email (Mimecast), Google Workspace, endpoints (CrowdStrike), and key SaaS apps, and investigate and respond to data exposure, whether from accidental oversharing, a compromised account, or insider misuse
  • Own security for Fleetio's use of AI: visibility into AI tool usage, identity and access for AI agents, guardrails for internal agents and automations, and AI detection and response (CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian, formerly AIDR)
  • Run vulnerability management for corporate assets, prioritizing by exploitability and holding owners to fix deadlines, and report on security posture with clear, honest metrics that help set program priorities

Your Experience

  • 5+ years of experience in security operations, detection and response, or security engineering, ideally at a SaaS company
  • Detection engineering and threat hunting in a SIEM (CrowdStrike Next-Gen SIEM or similar)
  • Security automation: building SOAR playbooks (CrowdStrike Fusion or similar) that connect identity, endpoint, email, and SaaS tools into a single response flow, with Python or PowerShell and REST APIs
  • Incident response from first triage through forensics, root cause, and follow-up across cloud, identity, and SaaS environments, including working with an MDR or managed SOC provider
  • Identity security with Okta or a similar provider: authentication policy, privileged access, and access reviews in a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 control environment
  • Endpoint security with CrowdStrike or similar, including macOS, plus device trust and endpoint query tooling
  • Email security (Mimecast or similar) and SaaS security posture management
  • Designing and running a DLP program: data classification, policy design and tuning across email, cloud collaboration, and endpoints, and investigating data exposure
  • Securing developer tooling and the software supply chain (IDE extensions, package registries, AI coding tools)
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including explaining risk to non-technical leaders

Considered a Plus

  • Experience securing a company's use of AI: AI tool governance, identity and access for agents, data-exposure and prompt-injection risk, and AI detection and response tooling (CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian/AIDR or similar)
  • Experience building AI agents, LLM-powered automations, or integrations (e.g., using tool/function calling or MCP) for security operations workflows
  • Experience using LLMs on real security alerts for triage, enrichment, and investigation

jobs.title: Compliance Engineer
jobs.description:
Compliance Engineer

About Playson

Playson builds premium casino games and platform solutions for operators worldwide. Our products reach millions of players across regulated markets, and we ship frequently - which means our certification and compliance evidence has to be as well-engineered as the games themselves.

We are hiring a Software Developer, Compliance, to own that engineering: a pipeline that lets us ship faster and safer, and a defence of the platform and the games that holds up in front of a lab, an ISO assessor, and a future SOC 2 auditor.

About the role

You are a software developer sitting inside compliance. You will build and continuously evolve a secure compliance pipeline so we can ship games and platform changes faster and safer - and you will be the technical person who defends what we shipped when an auditor, a certification lab, or a regulator asks.

The scope is not games alone. You will stand in front of game certification labs, and you will also defend the platform: ISO certification of our systems and the evidence work that leads into a future SOC 2 audit. In every case, the job is the same. You produce the proof. You walk the auditor through it. You answer the question that was asked, with the evidence that was requested, and you stop there.

You will own the technical side of game certification. You take a game math package from the review channel to the lab, you produce the evidence the lab needs - build hashes, PAR sheets, configuration snapshots, version manifests - and you answer the lab's technical questions yourself, without a developer sitting next to you. When a certificate comes back, you are the person who confirms every deficiency is closed before the game is allowed past the pre-release gate.

Between lab submissions, you treat the pipeline as a product. Manual evidence collection, one-off screenshots, and tribal knowledge are the things you replace. You automate controls, tighten the audit trail, and shorten the path from "ready to ship" to "ready to show an auditor" without weakening the bar. Faster and safer at the same time is the point of this role - not one at the expense of the other.

What we're looking for

  • You are a developer first. 3+ years writing production code, comfortable reading someone else's codebase and forming your own opinion about what it does. You are not a documentation coordinator who learned some technical words

  • Strong Node.js and TypeScript. Our game math packages, engine integration, rules and bets migrations, test suites, and compliance automation are all JavaScript-side. You will read game math code and verify that what it does matches what we told the lab it does - and you will write the tooling that makes that check repeatable

  • You know what it takes to build certified products. You have worked for an iGaming game provider, a lottery, or another business where products require certification. You understand how that shapes development, testing, and releases, and why the code and supporting evidence need to stay aligned.

  • You build pipelines, not checklists. You have taken a manual, high-stakes process and turned it into something engineered: automated evidence, versioned artefacts, gates that fail closed

  • You can read data and write queries. SQL against a production analytics store, log investigation, understanding a metrics pipeline well enough to tell a real control failure from a broken dashboard

  • Composure in front of an auditor. In a lab session, an ISO assessment, or a future SOC 2 walkthrough, you answer the question that was asked with the evidence that was requested. You communicate with auditors and certification labs precisely and factually. You provide complete evidence for the question or control being assessed, avoid speculation, and escalate regulatory interpretations to the Head of Compliance

  • You know where your authority ends. When a question moves from technical fact to regulatory interpretation or commercial consequence, you route it to the Head of Compliance instead of improvising

  • You write clearly and permanently. Compliance evidence is read years later by people who were not in the room. Your documentation has to survive that

  • You are comfortable saying no. You will be the person telling a squad, under release pressure, that their change does not pass the gate. That conversation needs to be calm, specific, and final

  • Precise by temperament. You check the version number rather than remembering it. You are not bored by an audit trail

Nice to have

  • Direct dealings with a certification lab (GLI, BMM, eCOGRA, iTech Labs, or similar) or a gaming regulator

  • Hands-on evidence work for ISO 27001, SOC 2, or an equivalent information-security audit

  • Understanding of RNG, RTP mathematics, and how statistical certification evidence is produced

  • Familiarity with multi-jurisdiction licensing (UKGC, MGA, and regulated EU and LatAm markets)

  • Observability and alerting tooling - Datadog or equivalent, including building automation on top of it rather than just reading dashboards

  • Experience with change-management controls, audit trails, and segregation-of-duties models

  • Incident response experience, particularly where the incident had a regulatory or audit dimension
